Four weeks after feedback, learners in the direct-corrections-on-grammar, metalinguistic-codes-on-grammar, and direct-corrections-on-grammar-and-nongrammar conditions showed significantly greater long-term grammatical accuracy than the no-feedback control (Bonilla López et al., 2018). The design is a strength—random assignment, five conditions, delayed posttest—yet cognitive load was measured by self-report rather than an online physiological index (Bonilla López et al., 2018).

content.text: Naturalistic work shifts attention from feedback type to learner uptake. In a naturalistic case study, AWE feedback tended to highlight rather than correct errors, and teacher feedback covered more error types (16) than AWE (8), although assignment differences may have driven this (Zhang & Hyland, 2018). The highly engaged learner outperformed the moderately engaged learner in her response to both sources of feedback and in improvements to her text (Zhang & Hyland, 2018). In an integrated approach combining automated, peer, and teacher feedback, 88% of 33 students submitted to the AWE system more than five times (M = 9.5, SD = 4.07), and most engaged behaviourally, affectively, and cognitively (Zhang & Hyland, 2021). The single-context case design limits generalizability (Zhang & Hyland, 2021).
